idea: Week three, from the story bank: written from the source, then corrected by two independent editors before voicing.
description: Himachal Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh had level income per person in 2023-24 (₹2,34,721 and ₹2,37,951). Yet 76.0% of men aged 15 to 49 in Himachal Pradesh had 10 or more years of school, against 59.5% in Andhra Pradesh. India's figure was 54.6%. Andhra Pradesh's was 47.9% in the earlier survey round.
Survey estimates from NFHS-6 (2023-24). Income here means state output per person, not what residents earn. Across states men's schooling mostly follows income. The table shows how much, not why.
source: Schooling: share of men aged 15 to 49 with 10 or more years of schooling, NFHS-6 (2023-24) state and India fact sheets, International Institute for Population Sciences (total, urban and rural columns; the NFHS-5 (2019-21) figure is printed beside it). 34 states and UTs ranked; Lakshadweep (small sample) is not ranked and Manipur has no NFHS-6 fact sheet. Income: per-capita net state domestic product, current prices, 2023-24, Reserve Bank of India, Handbook of Statistics on Indian States, Table 19 (33 states and UTs with data; National Statistical Office series).
